thread:
incident-bot: Pager: high error rate for inference endpoints in az1a — severity: P1 :rotating_light:

alex (oncall-sre): getting paged, seeing 5xxs and token latency spikes across multiple model routes. first alerted by synthetic checks.

lana (eng-runtime): thanks, I'm looking at runtime telemetry — 99th pct tail latency for gpt-13k up ~3x, lots of TCP connection resets from hosts in az1a.

alex (oncall-sre): confirming, NLB target health shows intermittent 502/504. traffic to az1a node pool dropping connections: `connreset` spikes.

rachel (eng-sre): checking host metrics — kernel rx drops and qdisc drops on the ENIs for a subset of hosts in az1a. AWS console showing increased RxError on 4 instances.

mike (eng-platform): provisioning spare capacity in eu-west-1 as temporary capacity is available. starting cross-zone steer plan.

jules (prod-support): any customer impact? getting inbound CS tickets about timeouts.

olivia (customer-ops): onboarded customers show 2–7% request failures, some with retries hitting rate limits. currently isolating customers with heavy KV cache requests.

lana (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: packet-level jitter on a subset of ENIs causing persistent connection resets which cause our serving processes to close kvcache streams and reinit, tanking tail latency. also seeing increased per-token CPU due to repeated KV cache cold starts.

alex (oncall-sre): immediate mitigation: 1) mark affected instances for drain, 2) shift new traffic out of az1a to other AZ in region, 3) enable short-term request-level retries with jitter/backoff. starting now.

deploy-bot: Routing change applied — traffic steering policy updated: az1a weight -> 10% (was 50%) at 1768890200.

mike (eng-platform): kicking off a rolling scale-up in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 to absorb load. autoscaler note: increase max pods on inference pool by +30% for 30m.

rachel (eng-sre): draining hosts: `kubectl annotate node ip-10-0-23-45 drain-immediate=true` then `cordon`. logs: one node shows kernel message `NETDEV WATCHDOG: eth0 (eni): transmit queue 0 timed out`.

lana (eng-runtime): temp mitigation: enable aggressive prefix caching for active sessions to reduce KV reads across the network. pushing config: `runtime.config.prefix_cache.enabled = true` and `prefix_cache.ttl=60s` for hot routes.

jules (prod-support): notifying impacted customers via status page — drafting message that we are routing traffic away from az1a and will update within 30m.

olivia (customer-ops): some enterprise customers require explicit acknowledgment. are we able to provide per-customer impact windows?

alex (oncall-sre): yes, collecting sample logs per-customer and percent errors. attaching quick counts: `curl -s http://metrics.internal/errcounts?az=az1a` -> 4.8% 5xx averaged over last 10m.

lana (eng-runtime): found pattern: connections that reset show TCP retransmits > 50 and latency spikes before reset. suspect noisy NIC firmware or host driver interacting with a particular ENA version.

mike (eng-platform): opening AWS support ticket (case id: 1234567890) and requesting NIC health scan + pcap capture on affected instances.

incident-bot: AWS case 1234567890 created by mike at 1768890305.

rachel (eng-sre): as a short-term protective measure, enabling connection-level backpressure: set proxy `max_inflight_per_connection=8` and `idle_timeout=15s` for clients to reduce retries amplifying failure.

lana (eng-runtime): also temporarily lowering model sequence length enforcement for heavy routes to reduce per-request resource use (non-invasive): `model.config.max_seq_override=2048` for gpt-13k route.

alex (oncall-sre): performing handoff to rachel at 1768890600 for continued mitigation; I'll be on-call for paging if it recurs. rachel acked.

rachel (eng-sre): acked. taking over coordination, will keep updates every 10m or on significant change.

mike (eng-platform): AWS responded: they see physical link anomalies on the AZ fabric side; suggested moving affected ENIs to different hosts (in-place ENI migration) or reprovisioning instances. we've scheduled instance reprovision for the 6 impacted hosts now.

lana (eng-runtime): reconfig traffic to prefer cached model variants for heavy customers to preserve quality while reducing load: enable `fallback_model=quantized-8bit` for routes with >2% error. will monitor quality metrics.

jules (prod-support): status page update posted: "We are experiencing elevated errors in AZ1a. Traffic is being steered to other AZs; engineering is investigating. Partial mitigation in progress." :information_source:

olivia (customer-ops): sending proactive notes to top 5 affected customers with ETA ~ 60m and mitigation steps.

rachel (eng-sre): reprovision actions in flight: `aws ec2 terminate-instances --instance-ids i-0abcde12345` for the 6 bad instances — autoscaling group will replace. expected new NICs within ~4–6 minutes per instance.

deploy-bot: Autoscaling group replace triggered at 1768891002.

alex (oncall-sre): quick sanity: synthetic runner now shows error rate down to 1.2% after steering, tail latency 99p reduced but still ~1.6x above baseline.

lana (eng-runtime): kvcache warmup happening — seeing steady decrease in cache misses. preparing to slowly increase az1a traffic weight if metrics remain stable.

rachel (eng-sre): first replaced host healthy at 1768891205, ENI errors cleared on that host.

mike (eng-platform): AWS confirmed NIC firmware mismatch on older host family; replacements are healthy. AWS is doing a cluster-level check for remaining hosts.

jules (prod-support): customers acknowledging the update, a few asked for postmortem timeline and RCA.

lana (eng-runtime): plan for next hours: 1) finish reprovision of all impacted hosts, 2) keep steering until 6 consecutive minutes of stable 99p latency, 3) roll back prefix_cache and model limits once kvcache and connection stability restored.

rachel (eng-sre): marking incident as "mitigating". creating incident doc in /incident-runbooks/ with initial timeline and affected customers list.

incident-bot: Incident state: MITIGATING at 1768891500. Pager channel remains open.

mike (eng-platform): follow-up action items assigned: upgrade NIC firmware baseline for that host class, add an ENI health monitor to export to dashboards, and add an automated temporary steer policy when rx_errors > X.

alex (oncall-sre): thanks team. i'll stay available for escalation. handing final note to rachel for postmortem lead.

rachel (eng-sre): taking postmortem lead. will post interim RCA in 24h and full postmortem after AWS completes hardware investigation.

jules (prod-support): closing loop on customer comms and collecting logs per-request for support attachments.

incident-bot: Incident update posted to status page at 1768891700. Next update scheduled in 30m unless state changes. :white_check_mark:
